title: [FSDP] World-size-one gradient division allocates a full-size temporary
body:
### Author's observation

Ascend NPU에서 FSDP world-size-one 구성의 backward 중 OOM을 관찰했습니다. 원인을 확인한 결과 gradient division이 (`reduce_output.copy_(reduce_scatter_input / gradient_divide_factor)`) degree가 1이어도 다음을 전체 크기 임시 텐서로 만들고 있어, 의미를 유지하면서 in-place 처리하여 Full-size 임시텐서를 수정하는 것이 필요하다고 판단했습니다.

### AI-assisted English summary

> The following English summary was prepared with an AI assistant to explain the author's observation above.
>
> In FSDP2 `foreach_reduce()`, a reduce-scatter group with world size one skips the collective. When `gradient_divide_factor` is set, the current world-size-one expression divides `reduce_scatter_input` out of place before copying the result into the already allocated `reduce_output`. The division therefore allocates another full-size tensor at the backward memory peak.
>
> A minimal regression check can configure a one-rank FSDP model with a custom gradient divide factor, run backward under `TorchDispatchMode`, and inspect the dispatched division operators. The current path dispatches an out-of-place `aten.div`; the world-size-one path should not require an additional full-size buffer for this scaling.

### Versions

> The original observation came from a 16-device DeepSeek-V4 training run on Ascend NPU where the relevant FSDP reduce-scatter group had world size one. A complete `collect_env.py` report from that remote run is not available in this macOS checkout.
>
> The inspected upstream source revision is `pytorch/pytorch@046f15d65a23d5a6683e0309ce202ba377e9c17c`.
>
> Related downstream report: https://gitcode.com/cann/torchtitan-npu/pull/684
